title: fix(plugin-grid): a rich-content cell keeps the grid's one-line row — the Studio Records grid and console lists draw every row (objectui#12480)
body:
Fixes #12480
Clause-②: no

## Root cause

The rows are not missing: they are drawn, below the fold of the grid's scroll box. One row is very tall.

- `data-table` keeps a cell to one line with `truncate` unless the column is authored `wrap: true`. `truncate` is nowrap + overflow hidden + ellipsis. It bounds inline content only. It never bounds the cell body's height.
- The three rich-content cell renderers (`markdown`, `html`, `richtext`, the `RICH_TEXT_FIELD_TYPES` table in `@object-ui/fields`) draw a block document: paragraphs, headings, lists. Blocks stack under nowrap.
- HotCRM's `crm_account` has a `description` markdown field. Its seed gives Acme Corporation a long multi-paragraph description. The Studio Records grid shows every non-system field as a column (37 here), so the Description column is in the grid, off-screen to the right.
- Result: Acme's row grows to the document's height (456 px in Chromium). Its visible cells are vertically centred in that row, which reads as "a tall empty band, then the row". The rows after it sit below the scroll box's bottom edge, and the footer still counts them.
- The committed screenshot fits this exactly: row 9 starts at y 586, and a 456 px row centred there puts its text at y 814. The screenshot shows it at y 815.

The trigger is the content, not the row count. The 8-row object in the card did not reproduce it because it has no long rich-content value. An 8-row object with one does the same thing (table below).

PR #12479 is not the cause: the screenshot's commit `cf430cd` is an ancestor of #12479's merge commit (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` exit 0).

## The fix

`ObjectGrid` (`packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx`). Every column passes through `applyColumnChrome`. That function now also runs a new step, `withOneLineRichText`. For a column whose field resolves to a rich-content renderer and which is not authored `wrap: true`, it wraps the renderer's output in a `line-clamp-1` box. The first line of the document shows; the rest is cut.

- The renderer itself is unchanged, so its sanitising pipeline stays the trust boundary.
- A column authored `wrap: true` still shows the whole document, as authored.
- The record-detail drawer resolves its renderers separately, so it still shows the full document.

Why not in `data-table`: it does not know field types. A generic height clamp there would also clip legitimate one-line widgets that are taller than one text line. Measured on the same harness: thumbnails 32 px, select badges 22 px, against a line height of 16 to 19.5 px.

Measured per type on the harness: only `markdown`, `html` and `richtext` exceed one line. Before the fix, at the first row: html 176 px and richtext 104 px. textarea, json, address, multi-select, file, image and code stay within 16–32 px. So the clamp covers the whole class.

## Browser readings (Chromium `/opt/pw-browsers/chromium`, 1280 x 900)

Scratch harness in `apps/console` (never committed, deleted after). It uses the real `ObjectView` (plugin-view) with `renderStudioGridList` as its `renderListView` slot, inside a `min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-auto` body like the Data pillar's `data-records-body`. A mock data source supplies `crm_account`-shaped fields, plus a `description` markdown field carrying the Acme description on the last row. The "console" rows mount `ListView` (plugin-list) directly with its default toolbar, which is the body the console's object list page renders. No backend ran.

| case | rows | before: tall row / rows inside the box | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Studio, plain text only (control) | 8 / 9 / 10 | none, all 41 px, 8/8, 9/9, 10/10 visible | not re-measured in the browser; the jsdom CONTROL pin holds it |
| Studio, one long markdown description | 8 | last row 456 px, 7 of 8 visible | all 41 px, 8 of 8 |
| Studio, one long markdown description | 9 | last row 456 px, 8 of 9 visible | all 41 px, 9 of 9 |
| Studio, one long markdown description | 10 | last row 456 px, 9 of 10 visible, table 873 px in a 642 px box | all 41 px, 10 of 10, table 458 px |
| console list body, same data | 8 / 9 / 10 | last row 456 px; 7/8, 8/9, 9/10 visible | all 36 px, 8/8, 9/9, 10/10 |

Triage's second question: **yes, console list pages show the same thing.** They render through the same `ObjectGrid`, and this fix covers both.

## Tests (head `256cd24d4`)

- New: `packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/ObjectGrid.richTextOneLine-12480.test.tsx` (jsdom does no layout, so these read the class contract and the row count).
  - 10 rows with a markdown, an html and a richtext column: 10 body rows; 30 clamps (`line-clamp-1`), one per rich cell; each document is drawn inside its clamp; the text column is not clamped.
  - `wrap: true` on the markdown column: no clamp, and the list is drawn.
  - CONTROL: an 8-row object with no rich-content column: 8 rows, no clamp, the cell still `truncate`s.
- Ablation (fix committed in `d4005d878`, mutated with objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs --hold` under an EXIT trap):
  - The guard line in `withOneLineRichText` was replaced by an unconditional `return col`. On disk: anchor count 1 to 0, marker count 0 to 1.
  - Result: the pin went red (1 failed / 2 passed), and the browser's console rows above went back to the 456 px row.
  - Restored with `git checkout HEAD`. `git diff HEAD` is 0 bytes, and the file's blob equals the HEAD blob (`887bcfcb3989`).
  - No dist step: the test imports `../ObjectGrid` by source path.
- `vitest run packages/plugin-grid/`: 216 files / 2015 tests passed (on `d4005d878`). The new pin plus `ObjectGrid.columnWrapForward.test.tsx`: 8 / 8 passed on `256cd24d4`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-grid type-check` (both `tsc` projects; the test project includes `src/**/*.test.tsx`): exit 0, after `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/plugin-grid^...' build` exit 0.
- No public export, prop or schema key changed, so the import-side packages owe no tests (declared, CI runs them).

## Gates

- `check:phantom-deps`, `self-import`, `unreferenced-sources`, `doc-example-readers`, `handler-key-reads`, `side-effects-array`, `element-data-source-declaration`, `spec-symbols`, `action-forward-parity`, `designer-field-key-parity`, `icon-record-names`, `i18n-keys`, `i18n-drift`, `i18n-designer-parity`, `control-bytes` and `new-line-citations`: all exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-fixed.mjs`, `check-changeset-presence.mjs` and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: exit 0.
- `check:spec-floors`: exit 1, its "no-artifact" prerequisite line (it wants a whole-workspace build). NOT MEASURED here. It is the known red on main (objectui#12334).
- Lint, narrowed to the 2 changed files (`eslint --no-inline-config --format json`). The test file has 0 errors. `ObjectGrid.tsx` has 1 error and 219 warnings; linted the same way, the base blob has 1 error and 215 warnings. The one error is the same pre-existing `react-hooks/static-components` far below the edit. The 4 new warnings are `no-explicit-any` on the new step's `col` / `value` / `row` / schema reads, the same spelling as its neighbour `withSortability`. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- **Content, not count.** The card's "8-row case is fine" is true only for an object with no long rich-content value. The pin's CONTROL keeps that case unchanged.
- **`wrap: true` keeps the full document.** A rich-content column authored `wrap: true` still grows its row to the whole document. That is the author's choice, and this change keeps it.
- **Not measured.**
  - The phone card layout (below 768 px). `ObjectGrid` resolves its own renderers there, so this change does not reach it.
  - Kanban and gallery cards, which draw the same renderers.
  - A dotted lookup-path column (no field definition here, so not clamped).
- **Merge.** `origin/main` was merged once more right before opening (`256cd24d4`, a merge commit). PR #12481's region of `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` is untouched: this diff does not edit that file.

Changeset: `.changeset/12480-studio-grid-missing-rows.md` (`@object-ui/plugin-grid` patch).
